what is esp in networking

esp stands for encapsulating security payload, and it is the part of the ipsec suite that actually protects the traffic. it gives you confidentiality by encrypting the payload of the ip packet, and integrity and authenticity through a message authentication code, so the receiver can tell both that nobody read it and that nobody altered it in transit. you see it most often behind vpns, where it is doing the heavy lifting for site to site tunnels. the spec itself is rfc 4303 if you want the exact field layout.

can you explain the first law of motion the way youd explain it to a five year old

It is the law of inertia, and the short version is that things carry on doing whatever they are already doing. If something is sitting still it stays sitting still until something pushes or pulls it. does strong consistency in dynamodb mean linearizable

Yes, that is what it amounts to. A strongly consistent read returns the most recent committed write, so what you get back reflects everything that had been written before the read was issued. That is the linearizable behaviour people mean when they use the word, as opposed to the eventually consistent reads which can hand you a slightly stale value depending on which replica answers you.
